name: Michaël Gharbi
current_role: Member of Technical Staff, OpenAI (previously co-founder and Chief Scientist, Reve)
profile: French computer-vision and graphics researcher (Ecole Polytechnique; PhD at MIT CSAIL under Fredo Durand) who was a Research Scientist at Adobe Research before co-founding image-generation startup Reve with Christian Cantrell, Taesung Park, Jon Watte and Mike Speiser, serving as Founder and Chief Scientist. His own site now lists him as a Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI.
interesting_fact: He co-authored 'Deep Bilateral Learning for Real-Time Image Enhancement' (SIGGRAPH 2017, with Google researchers) and the one-step diffusion 'Distribution Matching Distillation' papers (CVPR 2024 / NeurIPS 2024); a 2025 SIGGRAPH Asia paper he co-wrote won Best Paper.
deep_cut_fact: Outside graphics, he co-authored a 2018 Science Advances paper applying a convolutional neural network to earthquake detection and location (with Thibaut Perol and Marine Denolle), and contributed to the learned autoscheduler for the Halide image-processing language.
notes: Now at OpenAI per his personal site (date of move not stated) - his Reve stake/'founder' status may be outdated. Pure researcher, low media profile. His site lists a phone number - deliberately not recorded. Site notes the economist Sarah Gharbi is a different person.

name: Jake Loosararian
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Gecko Robotics (wall-climbing inspection robots + AI for critical infrastructure, Pittsburgh)
profile: Jake Loosararian started Gecko Robotics as a Grove City College engineering student after visiting a power plant losing millions per month to boiler downtime, and co-founded the company with his college roommate Troy Demmer in 2013. Gecko's robots and Cantilever AI software inspect boilers, tanks, pipelines and Navy ships; it raised a $125M Series D in June 2025 at a $1.25B valuation.
interesting_fact: Gecko was in Y Combinator's Winter 2016 batch, one of the first robotics companies YC backed, and now works with Fortune 100 energy, oil & gas and manufacturing firms as well as the US Air Force and US Navy.
deep_cut_fact: He built the first Gecko prototype in his college dorm room - a robot that could climb walls carrying ultrasonic sensors and cameras - then spent weeks on site in a dirty power-plant boiler adapting it until it found the plant's recurring failure.
notes: Excellent fit for an energy podcast (power-plant origin story, grid/energy infrastructure). Media-friendly: CNBC and Fortune founder-story pieces linked from Gecko's About page. Contact form has a 'Media/Press' option.

name: Tanner Runia
current_role: Co-founder and President, Awardco (employee recognition and rewards platform, Lindon, Utah)
profile: Tanner Runia is co-founder and President of Awardco, which he built with cousins Steve and Mike Sonnenberg. Awardco combines employee recognition with a zero-markup Amazon Business rewards catalogue; it raised a $165M Series B in May 2025 (Sixth Street Growth lead, with Spectrum Equity, General Catalyst and Ryan Smith) at a valuation above $1B.
interesting_fact: On the 2025 Series B, Runia stressed Awardco entered its next phase 'from a position of strength' as a cash-flow-positive, high-growth business; the company says it now serves 3,000+ organisations.
notes: Low public profile; no personal background found in press coverage (web search budget ran out before a deeper look). Best route is via Awardco; no published press email.
